circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281 km track located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, designed by Hermann Tilke to host the season-concluding Formula One race since 2009. It represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One venue, following Bahrain's circuit and preceding those established in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street course encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne that hosts the Formula One Australian Grand Prix each year, alongside the Supercars Championship and various supporting events. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 classification for racing facilities.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit has a storied history hosting the Austrian Grand Prix across two distinct eras. Originally constructed as the Österreichring, it held the race annually from 1970 to 1987 before undergoing reconstruction and renaming, eventually welcoming the grand prix back for a seven-year stint between 1997 and 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: Located along Baku Boulevard in Azerbaijan, this street circuit spans 6. 003 km, ranking as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One racing. It first hosted the European Grand Prix in 2016 before becoming a regular fixture on the calendar as the Azerbaijan Grand Prix starting in 2017.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Inaugurated in 2004, Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km track that hosts the annual Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix, marking the championship's first Middle Eastern venue. The facility accommodates various motorsport categories including drag racing, GP2 Series, and 24-hour endurance competitions, with a FIA Grade 1 certification and multiple circuit configurations available.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish motorsport venue features a balanced layout combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it a comprehensive test of driver and machine capabilities. The circuit holds an FIA Grade 1 classification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Situated in the Walloon region of Belgium near the town of Spa, this 7. 004 km circuit has been a fixture of Formula One racing since the sport's inaugural 1950 season. The venue currently hosts the Belgian Grand Prix annually, with consistent participation in the championship calendar from 1985 onwards apart from two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km temporary street circuit that hosts the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the venue has accommodated various motorsport competitions including world sportscar racing, Champ Car, and multiple NASCAR series throughout its history.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Nestled in Shanghai's Jiading district, this motorsport facility served as the home of the Chinese Grand Prix from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The venue has expanded its racing calendar to include electric racing events beginning in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Silverstone and Whittlebury in Northamptonshire, England, this racing circuit inaugurated the British Grand Prix in 1948 and subsequently hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After rotating with two rival venues between 1955 and 1986, the British Grand Prix became a permanent fixture at the track from 1987 onward, while the circuit also stages the British MotoGP round.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Mogyoród, is a 4. 381 km permanent circuit that hosted the inaugural Formula One Grand Prix held within the Eastern Bloc when racing commenced there in 1986. Built in just eight months starting from October 1985, faster than any other contemporary F1 venue, the track was constructed outside the city rather than as the originally envisioned street circuit in Budapest's central park.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located north of Milan in Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale di Monza is a 5. 793 km track constructed in 1922 as mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built racing circuit. Home to the Italian Grand Prix since 1949, it remains one of the few venues to continuously appear on the Formula One calendar from the sport's beginning, earning the nickname "Temple of Speed" for its extended straights and fast corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka International Racing Course is a 5. 807-kilometer Japanese motorsport venue operated by Honda Mobilityland in Mie Prefecture. The track, holding 155,000 spectators, is primarily renowned for hosting Formula One and Super Formula racing competitions.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, running alongside the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its collection of major casinos and hotels. The 3. 8-mile layout weaves past iconic venues such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, showcasing some of the city's most recognizable landmarks.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: This 4. 304 km Mexico City circuit honours brothers Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, both accomplished drivers who tragically died in racing accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The track returned to hosting Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix in 2015 after a 23-year absence, following earlier stints on a different configuration that concluded in 1992, with the event now branded as the Mexico City Grand Prix since 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens that measures 3. 363 miles and incorporates 19 corners, allowing qualifying speeds approaching 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One, the track joined the championship calendar in 2022 and has since become home to the Miami Grand Prix, with Formula E adopting a modified version of the layout beginning in the 2025-26 season.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street track that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts of Monaco, encircling the harbor area. It is officially known as Monte Carlo, reflecting that most of the circuit occupies the Monte Carlo neighborhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted the Dutch Grand Prix from 2021 until 2026. Known colloquially as "The Roller coaster in the Dunes," the circuit is characterized by dramatic elevation changes and steeply banked corners like Tarzan and Hugenholtz that wind through the seaside landscape.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a motorsport venue situated north of Doha in Qatar, stretching 5. 419 kilometers with a 1. 068-kilometer main straight and holding FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian racing venue in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace following his fatal aircraft accident eight years earlier. The counterclockwise circuit features additional karting facilities dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront in Jeddah. Since 2021, it has served as the venue for the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix, with the circuit also hosting an international electric racing championship event beginning in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's Marina Bay area, incorporating the Downtown Core and Kallang districts as it traverses city streets.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit features a balanced combination of extended straightaways and diverse corner designs, making it a comprehensive test of driver and vehicle capabilities. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 track that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside other major international racing series including MotoGP and the World Endurance Championship. Beyond its Formula One duties, the facility has hosted various motorsport events over the years, ranging from NASCAR to sports car racing and open-wheel competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a racing driver of Thai and British nationality who currently races for Williams in Formula One, representing Thailand.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has claimed two world championships in 2005 and 2006 during his tenure with Renault, along with 32 race victories over 23 seasons. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has distinguished himself in endurance racing by winning the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, two Le Mans 24-hour races with Toyota, and the 2019 Daytona 24-hour event, making him the sole driver to have achieved success in both Formula One's world championship and the world endurance championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli secured the Formula One World Drivers' Championship with Mercedes in 2026, setting a record as the sport's youngest champion. Since entering the series in 2025, he has claimed nine race victories.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabi Bortoleto competes in Formula One, currently representing Audi in the championship.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: The Finnish driver competes for Cadillac in Formula One and has achieved two runner-up championship finishes during his time with Mercedes in 2019 and 2020. Across his 13-season career, he has claimed 10 Grand Prix victories.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine motorsport competitor currently racing in Formula One with Alpine.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian racing driver, holds a reserve driver position with Haas while competing in prototype racing for AF Corse in the Asian Le Mans Series. He has made seven Formula One starts between 2024 and 2025, following earlier stints in the European Le Mans Series.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The driver achieved a career highlight by winning the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Hadjar is a French-Algerian racing driver who represents France in Formula One competition with Red Bull Racing.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: British driver Lewis Hamilton currently races for Ferrari after achieving unprecedented success throughout his Formula One career, including a record-tying seven world championship titles that he shares with Michael Schumacher. His accomplishments encompass the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races in Formula One for Audi. Beyond his single-seater career, he has achieved success in endurance motorsport, notably winning the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a racing driver from New Zealand, currently drives for Racing Bulls in Formula One.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Monaco-born Charles Leclerc currently drives for Ferrari in Formula One, where he has claimed nine race victories throughout his career. He came closest to the world championship in 2022, finishing as runner-up in the standings while representing the Italian team.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Danish driver Kevin Magnussen, known as K-Mag, recently concluded his second stint in Formula One, which spanned from 2022 to 2024, following an earlier period in the sport from 2014 to 2020. He has since transitioned to endurance racing, currently representing BMW as a factory driver in the FIA World Endurance Championship with WRT.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver, clinched the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship while competing for McLaren, adding to his tally of 14 race victories accumulated over his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: French driver Esteban Ocon recently drove for Haas in Formula One after previously claiming victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while competing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio Pérez is a Mexican driver currently racing in Formula One for Cadillac. The experienced competitor finished as runner-up in the 2023 championship while driving for Red Bull and has claimed six Grand Prix victories during his 15-year career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, having claimed nine Grand Prix victories since joining the grid four seasons ago.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo is an Australian driver who competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, earning the nickname "the Honey Badger" during his racing career. He secured eight Grand Prix victories throughout his tenure in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: George Russell represents Mercedes in Formula One competition as a British driver. He has claimed victory in eight Grand Prix races throughout his career spanning eight seasons.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024. He has since transitioned to competing in the FIA World Endurance Championship, where he will drive for Ford after previously racing in the LMGT3 category with Proton Competition.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Canadian driver Lance Stroll currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One. Known by his first and middle names in the sport, he has established himself as a competitor on the grid.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese motorsport competitor, transitioned to a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls after spending five seasons as a full-time Formula One driver from 2021 through 2025.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Max Verstappen is a Dutch-Belgian driver competing for Red Bull Racing who has claimed four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024. The 12-season veteran has accumulated 74 Grand Prix victories throughout his Formula One career.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is China's sole Formula One competitor to date, having raced in the sport from 2022 through 2024. He currently holds a reserve driver position with Cadillac in the championship.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Operating from Enstone since 2021 under the Alpine banner, this French-backed outfit functioned as Renault's factory racing division, inheriting the legacy of the Renault F1 Team. The squad maintained its works status throughout its tenure until Renault's withdrawal from the championship concluded at the end of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British manufacturer, has held multiple identities throughout its involvement in Formula One. The squad currently competes under the Aston Martin Aramco banner through AMR GP Limited.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari, stands as Formula One's longest-established and most accomplished team, having participated in every World Championship season since the sport's inception in 1950. Known colloquially as "the Prancing Horse" after their iconic emblem, the team remains the benchmark for longevity and success in Grand Prix racing.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American-licensed Formula One outfit founded by NASCAR team proprietor Gene Haas, the team competed for the first time during the 2016 season. Leadership passed to Ayao Komatsu in early 2024 following the departure of Guenther Steiner, who had directed operations since the team's establishment in 2014.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: This Swiss engineering firm, established in 1970 by Peter Sauber, initially built sports cars and achieved notable endurance racing success including a 1989 Le Mans victory. After joining Formula One in 1993 as an independent manufacturer, the team competed for over three decades before ceasing operations in 2025, ranking among the sport's longest-serving constructors. The company and its infrastructure were purchased by Audi AG in 2024 to serve as the foundation for Audi's Formula One programme.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing Limited is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at the McLaren Technology Centre in Woking. Operating as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group under Mumtalakat Holding Company's ownership, the team competes in the sport's top motorseries.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 through team ownership and engine supply, with its current iteration, Mercedes-AMG Petronas, based in Brackley and operating under a German licence. The team underwent a significant ownership restructuring in January 2022 when Ineos joined as an equal partner with Mercedes-Benz Group and team principal Toto Wolff, each holding one-third stakes. Mercedes-affiliated teams are traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows" due to their historic silver livery.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that commenced competition in 2024 as part of Red Bull's two-team structure. Based in Faenza with operations near its sister team in Milton Keynes, the squad operates as the second entity under Austrian ownership alongside Red Bull Racing.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that commenced operations in 2024 as Red Bull GmbH's second factory team. Headquartered in Faenza with an additional facility near Milton Keynes, the squad operates alongside Red Bull Racing as part of the Austrian conglomerate's dual-team structure in the championship.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, an Austrian-licensed team headquartered in England, has been a Formula One competitor since 2005 as part of Red Bull GmbH's motorsport operations. Under Christian Horner's leadership from inception through 2024, the team established itself as a major force in the championship before Laurent Mekies took over management responsibilities in 2025.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, a British Formula One constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, operates from its Grove, Oxfordshire headquarters. The team emerged following Williams's previous unsuccessful F1 venture and will compete in 2026 as Atlassian Williams F1 Team.
